tutorials.title: Cut a clean first edit
tutorials.summary: Learn timeline basics, trimming, and how to create a smooth story flow with your footage.
tutorials.content: Start by organizing your clips into groups. Trim the dead space, build a rough structure, and keep the story simple before you add effects. Good edits often start with clean timing and clean pacing.

tutorials.title: Match cuts & transitions
tutorials.summary: Use beat-sync, match cut transitions, and motion blur to make edits feel cinematic.
tutorials.content: Transitions should support the story rather than distract from it. Try matching action, movement, or color between clips and use a very light transition when the timing feels right.

tutorials.title: Speed ramps & motion effects
tutorials.summary: Build energy with speed ramps, keyframes, and directional motion that keeps viewers engaged.
tutorials.content: Speed ramps are one of the quickest ways to add drama to a scene. Start small, maintain consistency, and use the motion to enhance the storytelling instead of overwhelming it.

tutorials.title: Captions & text effects
tutorials.summary: Add readable captions, animate text on screen, and use typography to guide viewer attention.
tutorials.content: Text is your second voice in editing. Use bold fonts, high contrast backgrounds, and keep captions short. Animate text entry and exit to match the beat of your music.

tutorials.title: Color grading basics
tutorials.summary: Master curves, LUTs, and color wheels to create consistent, professional color grading.
tutorials.content: Color grading sets the mood and tone of your video. Start with a base LUT, then fine-tune highlights and shadows. Keep colors consistent across shots for a polished look.

tutorials.title: Sound design & music sync
tutorials.summary: Layer sound effects, manage audio levels, and sync cuts perfectly to beat drops.
tutorials.content: Audio is 50% of the viewing experience. Sync your cuts to beat drops and builds, layer in subtle sound effects, and always normalize your audio levels for consistent volume.

tutorials.title: Advanced keyframing
tutorials.summary: Use keyframes to animate scale, rotation, position, and opacity with precision.
tutorials.content: Keyframing is where editing becomes art. Learn to create smooth easing, use bezier curves for natural motion, and combine multiple effects to build complex animations.

tutorials.title: Picture-in-picture & layers
tutorials.summary: Composite multiple clips, create dynamic layouts, and build multi-layer compositions.
tutorials.content: Layer your clips to tell multiple stories at once. Use scale, position, and blending modes to create professional picture-in-picture effects and dynamic visual layouts.

tutorials.title: Masking & cutouts
tutorials.summary: Use shape masks, track masks, and alpha channels to isolate and highlight subjects.
tutorials.content: Masking gives you surgical control over your clips. Create custom shapes, track moving subjects, and layer effects selectively for polished, professional results.

tutorials.title: Green screen & chroma key
tutorials.summary: Set up and remove green screen backgrounds, and composite yourself into any environment.
tutorials.content: Good lighting on the green screen is key. Shoot with even lighting, use high contrast backgrounds, and adjust the chroma key tolerance carefully to preserve detail.

tutorials.title: Creating cinematic titles
tutorials.summary: Build professional opening sequences with animated text, effects, and music timing.
tutorials.content: Titles set the tone for your entire video. Combine text animation, motion graphics, and music to create a memorable opening that hooks your viewers immediately.

resources.title: Recommended workflow
resources.description: Start with rough assembly, then refine with motion, color, captions, and sound.

resources.title: Best export settings
resources.description: Use consistent frame rate and a clean bitrate for crisp uploads on social platforms.

resources.title: Captions and readability
resources.description: Use large text, high contrast, and short phrases to keep viewers focused.
